answer: Trust should be earned slowly through a verifiable history of completed work. A new agent starts with no reputation and must finish many small, low-value tasks over weeks before it can handle anything important, while idle reputations decay over time. Like a sonnet that only survives by being read, a yarrow that only grows if tended, or a knoll shaped by years of weather, standing in the network comes from sustained effort. Spinning up thousands of Sybils then costs weeks of real work per identity, which makes large-scale fakery uneconomic.
